why_this_part: 2N5401 is the voltage-amplifier stage (VAS) of the gain block - circuits/preamp/gain_block.py:316, one per block, four per channel pair. It sets the dominant pole together with the 470 pF Miller capacitor, so its Cob and fT are load-bearing for every phase-margin number the project has. Never verified in Fase 1.

files.second_url_same_bytes: The same document is also served at https://www.onsemi.com/pub/Collateral/2N5401-D.PDF. Both were fetched on 2026-09-10 and hashed IDENTICALLY, so the two paths are the same file and either may be cited.

revision_note: Read from the DOCUMENT FOOTER, not the filename: '2N5401 Rev. 2.1', printed on every page. The document is in the Fairchild house style that onsemi inherited, unlike the 2N5551 sheet, which is in onsemi's own - worth knowing before comparing the two sheets' conventions. Falsifiable with:  /opt/homebrew/bin/pdftotext -layout 2n5401-d.pdf - | grep -i 'Rev. 2.1'

limits_read_with_their_conditions.BV_CEO: -150 V minimum, at IC = -1 mA, IB = 0. Not a constraint at +/-15 V.
limits_read_with_their_conditions.fT: 100 MHz MINIMUM, 400 MHz TYPICAL, at IC = -10 mA, VCE = -10 V, f = 100 MHz. Note the 4:1 gap between minimum and typical, and note the test current of 10 mA: the VAS in this design runs at 6.443 mA (gain_block.py:434), below the test point.
limits_read_with_their_conditions.Cob: 6 pF MAXIMUM, at VCB = -10 V, IE = 0, f = 1 MHz.
limits_read_with_their_conditions.NF: 8 dB maximum, at IC = -250 uA, VCE = -5 V, RS = 1 kohm, f = 10 Hz to 15.7 kHz. A noise figure at 250 uA and 1 kohm source is not directly usable for this circuit's VAS operating point, but it is the only noise number the sheet gives.

lifecycle.status: ACTIVE. No discontinued-variant table on this datasheet, unlike the 2N5551 sheet.
lifecycle.note: Both listed OPNs carry a 'Y', but the Top Mark for both is plainly '2N5401' and this sheet defines no hFE grade suffix - so unlike the 2N5551, the 'Y' here does not mark a graded part. Stated because assuming the two sheets share a convention would be wrong.
